page: Microsoft Azure M8-4ms is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the MS server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8280M cores with hyper-threading enabled on the x86_64 architecture. The processor operates at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz and includes a 38 MB L3 cache. This instance is equipped with an exceptionally high memory capacity of 219.0 GB, yielding approximately 54.69 GB of RAM per core. It also includes 262 GB of local storage and is premium storage capable, though it does not bundle any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate that the M8-4ms prioritizes memory capacity over raw compute speed and memory bandwidth. The single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the poor to weak categories, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 1970.0 and a passmark CPU score of 3277.47. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth at 17.71 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 17.19 GB/sec. These metrics reveal a clear tradeoff: while the instance provides massive memory density, it is not designed for high-throughput computational tasks or high-speed data transfers.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the M8-4ms offers a highly specialized hardware profile, providing a massive memory footprint relative to its low vCPU count. This makes it a qualitatively cost-effective choice for workloads that require large memory capacities but have low CPU utilization requirements. It is well-suited for hosting large in-memory databases, caching layers such as Redis, and enterprise applications with high memory demands but moderate processing needs.
